questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The molecule with a maximum boiling point is
questions.solution:
The boiling point of a compound depends on the strength of its intermolecular forces.

Molecules containing $-\text{OH}$ groups can form intermolecular hydrogen bonds, which are significantly stronger than the dipole-dipole interactions and London dispersion forces present in alkyl halides. Therefore, alcohols generally have higher boiling points than alkyl halides of comparable molecular mass.

Among the given options:
$\text{CH}_3 - \text{CH}_2 - \text{Br}$ and $\text{CH}_3 - \text{CH}_2 - \text{CH}_2 - \text{Br}$ are alkyl halides and do not exhibit hydrogen bonding.
$\text{CH}_3 - \text{C}(\text{CH}_3)(\text{Cl}) - \text{OH}$ has one $-\text{OH}$ group, allowing for intermolecular hydrogen bonding.
$\text{CH}_3 - \text{CH}(\text{OH}) - \text{CH}_2 - \text{CH}_2 - \text{OH}$ (a diol) contains two $-\text{OH}$ groups per molecule. This allows for a more extensive network of intermolecular hydrogen bonds compared to a monohydric alcohol.

Due to the presence of two hydroxyl groups and the resulting extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonding, $\text{CH}_3 - \text{CH}(\text{OH}) - \text{CH}_2 - \text{CH}_2 - \text{OH}$ has the maximum boiling point.

Answer: $\text{CH}_3 - \text{CH}(\text{OH}) - \text{CH}_2 - \text{CH}_2 - \text{OH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following is a suitable method for preparation of ether?
options: Reacting sodium methoxide and tertiary butyl bromide
Reacting sodium tertiarybutoxide and methyl bromide
Reacting methyl alcohol and methyl bromide
questions.solution:
Williamson ether synthesis is an $S_N2$ reaction between an alkoxide ion and an alkyl halide. For the successful preparation of an ether, the alkyl halide must be primary or methyl, as secondary and tertiary alkyl halides tend to undergo elimination reactions in the presence of strong bases (alkoxides) to form alkenes.

Reacting sodium methoxide with tertiary butyl bromide (a $3^{\circ}$ alkyl halide) will predominantly yield isobutylene (an alkene) due to elimination.

Reacting sodium tertiarybutoxide with methyl bromide (a methyl halide) will successfully yield methyl tert-butyl ether, as methyl halides cannot undergo elimination and are highly reactive towards $S_N2$ substitution.

Therefore, reacting sodium tertiarybutoxide and methyl bromide is the suitable method.

Answer: Reacting sodium tertiarybutoxide and methyl bromide

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the product obtained when Grignard reagent reacts with alkyl cyanide followed by acid hydrolysis.
questions.solution:
Grignard reagents ($R'MgX$) react with alkyl cyanides ($R-C\equiv N$) to form an imine salt intermediate.

$R-C\equiv N + R'MgX \rightarrow R-C(R')=NMgX$

Upon acid hydrolysis, the imine salt is converted into a ketone.

$R-C(R')=NMgX + H_3O^+ \rightarrow R-C(=O)-R' + NH_3 + Mg(OH)X$

Thus, the final product obtained is a ketone.

Answer: a ketone

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Acetaldehyde, when heated in the presence of sodium hydroxide and iodine forms
questions.solution:
Acetaldehyde ($CH_3CHO$) contains a $CH_3-CO-$ group, so it undergoes the iodoform reaction when heated with iodine and sodium hydroxide.

The reaction proceeds as follows:

$CH_3CHO + 3I_2 + 4NaOH \xrightarrow{\Delta} CHI_3 + HCOONa + 3NaI + 3H_2O$

The products formed are iodoform ($CHI_3$) as a yellow precipitate and sodium formate ($HCOONa$).

Answer: Sodium formate

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following reactions is an example of a disproportionation reaction?
questions.solution:
A disproportionation reaction is a redox reaction in which the same substance undergoes both oxidation and reduction simultaneously.

In the Cannizzaro reaction, aldehydes lacking $\alpha$-hydrogens undergo self-oxidation and self-reduction in the presence of a concentrated base.

One molecule of the aldehyde is reduced to the corresponding alcohol, while another molecule is oxidized to the salt of the corresponding carboxylic acid.

For example: $2HCHO + NaOH \rightarrow HCOONa + CH_3OH$

Here, formaldehyde is oxidized to sodium formate and reduced to methanol. Thus, the Cannizzaro reaction is an example of a disproportionation reaction.

Wolf-Kishner and Clemmensen reductions are purely reduction reactions, whereas Aldol condensation is a condensation reaction.

Answer: Cannizzaro reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the product obtained when RCN is treated with sodium and alcohol.
questions.solution:
The reduction of alkyl cyanides (nitriles) with sodium and alcohol is known as the Mendius reduction.

In this reaction, the cyano group ($-\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$) is reduced to a primary amine group ($-\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$).

$\text{R-C}\equiv\text{N} + 4[\text{H}] \xrightarrow{\text{Na/C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}} \text{R-CH}_2\text{-NH}_2$

The product obtained is a primary amine, $\text{RCH}_2\text{NH}_2$.

Answer: $\text{RCH}_2\text{NH}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of following amines exhibits carbylamine test?
questions.solution:
The carbylamine test is a characteristic test for primary amines.

When a primary amine is heated with chloroform and alcoholic potassium hydroxide, it forms an isocyanide (carbylamine) which has a characteristic foul smell.

The reaction is given by:

$R-NH_2 + CHCl_3 + 3KOH \rightarrow R-NC + 3KCl + 3H_2O$

Secondary and tertiary amines do not give this test.

Answer: Primary amine

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The secondary structure of protein is determined by
questions.solution:
The secondary structure of a protein refers to the shape in which a long polypeptide chain can exist.

They are found to exist in two different types of structures, namely $\alpha$-helix and $\beta$-pleated sheet structures.

These structures arise due to the regular folding of the backbone of the polypeptide chain due to hydrogen bonding between the $-\text{C}=\text{O}$ and $-\text{NH}-$ groups of the peptide bonds.

Therefore, the secondary structure of a protein is determined by hydrogen bonds.

Answer: hydrogen bond

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The reaction of glucose with acetic Anhydride, confirms the
questions.solution:
Glucose reacts with acetic anhydride to form glucose pentaacetate.

The formation of the pentaacetate derivative indicates that there are five hydroxyl ($-\text{OH}$) groups present in a molecule of glucose.

Since glucose is a stable compound, these five hydroxyl groups must be attached to five different carbon atoms.

Answer: presence of five hydroxyl group

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the shape of $\text{IF}_5$ molecule from the following options.
questions.solution:
The central atom is Iodine (I), which has $7$ valence electrons.

It forms $5$ single bonds with $5$ Fluorine (F) atoms.

Number of bond pairs = $5$

Number of lone pairs = $\dfrac{7 - 5}{2} = 1$

Total number of electron pairs = $5 + 1 = 6$

The hybridization of the central atom is $sp^3d^2$, which corresponds to an octahedral electron geometry.

Due to the presence of $5$ bond pairs and $1$ lone pair, the molecular shape is square pyramidal.

Answer: Square pyramidal

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the rate constant?
options: It is proportionality constant in rate law that relates reaction rate to reactant concentrations.
It is independent of concentration of reactant.
Greater the value of rate constant slower is the reaction.
questions.solution:
According to the rate law, the rate of a reaction is given by $\text{Rate} = k[\text{Reactants}]^{n}$.

Here, $k$ is the rate constant, which is a proportionality constant relating the reaction rate to the reactant concentrations.

The rate constant $k$ is independent of the initial concentration of the reactants but depends on the temperature as given by the Arrhenius equation $k = A e^{-E_a/RT}$.

From the rate law, it is evident that the rate of the reaction is directly proportional to the rate constant $k$. Therefore, a greater value of the rate constant implies a faster reaction, not a slower one.

Hence, the statement 'Greater the value of rate constant slower is the reaction' is incorrect.

Answer: Greater the value of rate constant slower is the reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The rate constant for a first order reaction is $60 \text{ s}^{-1}$. How much time will it take to reduce the concentration of the reactant to $1/20^{\text{th}}$ of its initial value?
questions.solution:
For a first order reaction, the time required is given by the integrated rate equation:

$t = \dfrac{2.303}{k} \log \left( \dfrac{[R]_0}{[R]} \right)$

Given $k = 60 \text{ s}^{-1}$ and the final concentration $[R] = \dfrac{[R]_0}{20}$.

Substituting the values into the equation:

$t = \dfrac{2.303}{60} \log \left( \dfrac{[R]_0}{\dfrac{[R]_0}{20}} \right)$

$t = \dfrac{2.303}{60} \log(20)$

Using $\log(20) = \log(2 \times 10) = \log 2 + \log 10 = 0.3010 + 1 = 1.3010$:

$t = \dfrac{2.303 \times 1.3010}{60}$

$t = \dfrac{2.9962}{60}$

$t \approx 0.0499 \text{ s}$

Answer: $0.0499$ s

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A first order reaction complete $60$% in $20$ minutes. How long will the reaction take to complete $84$%?
questions.solution:
For a first order reaction, the rate constant is given by $k = \dfrac{2.303}{t} \log\left(\dfrac{a}{a-x}\right)$

For $60\%$ completion in $20$ minutes:

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{20} \log\left(\dfrac{100}{100-60}\right) = \dfrac{2.303}{20} \log(2.5)$

For $84\%$ completion in time $t$:

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{t} \log\left(\dfrac{100}{100-84}\right) = \dfrac{2.303}{t} \log(6.25)$

Equating the two expressions for $k$:

$\dfrac{1}{20} \log(2.5) = \dfrac{1}{t} \log(2.5^2)$

$\dfrac{1}{20} \log(2.5) = \dfrac{2}{t} \log(2.5)$

$t = 40$ min

Answer: $40$ min

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of drug the aspirin is?
questions.solution:
Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) is a non-narcotic analgesic. It is widely used to relieve minor aches and pains, and also has antipyretic (fever-reducing) and anti-inflammatory properties.

Therefore, aspirin is classified as an analgesic.

Answer: Analgesic

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Which of the following hydrides of Group $16$ elements has highest reducing property?
questions.solution:
The reducing property of Group $16$ hydrides depends on the ease with which they can release hydrogen atoms.

As we move down the group from oxygen to tellurium, the atomic size of the central atom increases.

This leads to an increase in the $E-\text{H}$ bond length ($E = \text{O, S, Se, Te}$) and a corresponding decrease in the bond dissociation enthalpy.

Due to the lowest bond dissociation enthalpy among the given options, $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$ releases hydrogen most easily.

Therefore, the reducing property increases in the order: $\text{H}_2\text{O} \lt \text{H}_2\text{S} \lt \text{H}_2\text{Se} \lt \text{H}_2\text{Te}$.

Hence, $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$ has the highest reducing property.

Answer: $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In a complex compound, central metal ion is
questions.solution:
In a complex compound, the central metal ion accepts one or more electron pairs from the surrounding ligands to form coordinate covalent bonds.

According to the Lewis theory of acids and bases, an electron pair acceptor is defined as a Lewis acid, while an electron pair donor is defined as a Lewis base.

Therefore, the central metal ion acts as a Lewis acid.

Answer: Lewis acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the hybridization in central metal of $[\text{Fe}(\text{CO})_5]$ complex.
questions.solution:
In $[Fe(CO)_5]$, the central metal atom is $Fe$ and its oxidation state is $0$.

The ground state electronic configuration of $Fe$ is $[Ar] 3d^6 4s^2$.

$CO$ is a strong field ligand, which causes the pairing of electrons.

The two $4s$ electrons shift to the $3d$ subshell and pair up, resulting in a $3d^8$ configuration. Four $3d$ orbitals are completely filled and one $3d$ orbital is left empty.

To accommodate the five electron pairs from the five $CO$ ligands, one $3d$, one $4s$, and three $4p$ orbitals hybridize.

Therefore, the hybridization is $dsp^3$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why zinc does not exhibit variable oxidation states?
questions.solution:
The atomic number of zinc is $30$.

The electronic configuration of zinc is $[Ar] 3d^{10} 4s^{2}$.

Zinc loses two electrons from the $4s$ subshell to form $Zn^{2+}$ ion, which has a stable $[Ar] 3d^{10}$ configuration.

Since the $3d$ subshell is completely filled and highly stable, it does not lose any further electrons.

Therefore, zinc does not exhibit variable oxidation states due to its completely filled $3d$ subshell.

Answer: Completely filled $3d$ subshell

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the set of paramagnetic ions among the following.
questions.solution:
Paramagnetic ions are those that contain at least one unpaired electron in their electronic configuration.

Writing the outer electronic configurations of the given ions:
$\text{V}^{+2}$: $[\text{Ar}] 3d^{3}$ (3 unpaired electrons, paramagnetic)
$\text{Co}^{+2}$: $[\text{Ar}] 3d^{7}$ (3 unpaired electrons, paramagnetic)
$\text{Ti}^{+4}$: $[\text{Ar}] 3d^{0}$ (0 unpaired electrons, diamagnetic)

$\text{Ni}^{+2}$: $[\text{Ar}] 3d^{8}$ (2 unpaired electrons, paramagnetic)
$\text{Cu}^{+2}$: $[\text{Ar}] 3d^{9}$ (1 unpaired electron, paramagnetic)
$\text{Zn}^{+2}$: $[\text{Ar}] 3d^{10}$ (0 unpaired electrons, diamagnetic)

$\text{Ti}^{+2}$: $[\text{Ar}] 3d^{2}$ (2 unpaired electrons, paramagnetic)
$\text{Cu}^{+2}$: $[\text{Ar}] 3d^{9}$ (1 unpaired electron, paramagnetic)
$\text{Mn}^{+3}$: $[\text{Ar}] 3d^{4}$ (4 unpaired electrons, paramagnetic)

$\text{Sc}^{+3}$: $[\text{Ar}] 3d^{0}$ (0 unpaired electrons, diamagnetic)
$\text{Ti}^{+3}$: $[\text{Ar}] 3d^{1}$ (1 unpaired electron, paramagnetic)
$\text{V}^{+3}$: $[\text{Ar}] 3d^{2}$ (2 unpaired electrons, paramagnetic)

The set containing only paramagnetic ions is $\text{Ti}^{+2}, \text{Cu}^{+2}, \text{Mn}^{+3}$.

Answer: $\text{Ti}^{+2}, \text{Cu}^{+2}, \text{Mn}^{+3}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the function of salt bridge.
questions.solution:
A salt bridge is a U-shaped tube containing an inert electrolyte in a gel-like substance.

Its primary functions are to complete the electrical circuit by connecting the two half-cells and to maintain the electrical neutrality of the solutions in the two half-cells.

Therefore, its function is to connect two half cells.

Answer: To connect two half cells.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements is true about the voltaic cell?
options: It converts chemical energy into electrical energy.
It converts electrical energy into chemical energy.
The anode of voltaic cells is positive.
The cathode of voltaic cell is negative.
questions.solution:
A voltaic cell (or galvanic cell) is an electrochemical cell that uses a spontaneous chemical reaction to generate an electric current. Therefore, it converts chemical energy into electrical energy.

In a voltaic cell, oxidation occurs at the anode, making it the negative electrode, while reduction occurs at the cathode, making it the positive electrode. An electrolytic cell, on the other hand, converts electrical energy into chemical energy.

Answer: It converts chemical energy into electrical energy.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements is correct regarding electrolysis of molten NaCl?
options: Pale green $\text{Cl}_2$ gas released at anode
Molten silvery white sodium is deposited at cathode
Decomposition of NaCl into Na metal and $\text{Cl}_2$ gas
questions.solution:
During the electrolysis of molten $\text{NaCl}$, the ions present are $\text{Na}^+$ and $\text{Cl}^-$.

At the cathode (reduction):
$\text{Na}^+ + e^- \rightarrow \text{Na}(l)$
Since the operating temperature is much higher than the melting point of sodium, molten silvery-white sodium metal is deposited at the cathode.

At the anode (oxidation):
$2\text{Cl}^- \rightarrow \text{Cl}_2(g) + 2e^-$
Pale green chlorine gas is liberated at the anode.

Since both statements A and B correctly describe the observations at the respective electrodes during the electrolysis process, the correct choice is both A and B.

Answer: Both options A and B

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: At $298$ K, the specific conductance ($\kappa$) of a $0.0020$ M NaCl solution is $2.50 \times 10^{-4} \text{ S cm}^{-1}$. Calculate the molar conductivity ($\Lambda_m$) of the solution in $\text{S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution:
Given:

$\kappa = 2.50 \times 10^{-4} \text{ S cm}^{-1}$

$C = 0.0020 \text{ M}$

The molar conductivity $\Lambda_m$ is given by the formula:

$\Lambda_m = \dfrac{\kappa \times 1000}{C}$

Substituting the given values:

$\Lambda_m = \dfrac{2.50 \times 10^{-4} \times 1000}{0.0020}$

$\Lambda_m = \dfrac{0.250}{0.0020}$

$\Lambda_m = 125 \text{ S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $125$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a green alternative for dry cleaning solvents?
questions.solution:
Tetrachloroethene (perchloroethylene) was traditionally used as a solvent for dry cleaning. However, it contaminates groundwater and is a suspected carcinogen.

To minimize environmental pollution and health hazards, green chemistry principles have led to the replacement of halogenated solvents with liquefied or supercritical $\text{CO}_2$ along with a suitable detergent.

Using supercritical $\text{CO}_2$ is a greener alternative as it is non-toxic, non-flammable, and does not contaminate groundwater.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of isomerism is exhibited by neopentane?
questions.solution:
Neopentane ($C_5H_{12}$) is an isomer of pentane.

The isomers of pentane are n-pentane, isopentane, and neopentane.

These compounds have the same molecular formula but differ in the arrangement of their carbon skeleton (straight chain versus branched chain).

Therefore, neopentane exhibits chain isomerism.

Answer: chain

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The major product 'B' in the below mentioned reaction is-
questions.solution:
The given reactant is 2-bromopropane ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{Br})-\text{CH}_3$).

When 2-bromopropane is treated with alcoholic KOH and heated, it undergoes dehydrohalogenation ($\beta$-elimination) to form propene (A).
$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{Br})-\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{Alc. KOH, } \Delta} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$

Next, propene (A) reacts with HBr in the absence of peroxide. This is an electrophilic addition reaction that follows Markovnikov's rule. The negative part of the addendum ($\text{Br}^-$) attaches to the carbon atom of the double bond that has fewer hydrogen atoms.
$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 + \text{HBr} \xrightarrow{\text{Peroxide absent}} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{Br})-\text{CH}_3$

Thus, the major product 'B' is 2-bromopropane.

Answer: 2-Bromopropane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Wurtz reaction is NOT possible with
questions.solution:
Wurtz reaction is used for the preparation of higher alkanes from alkyl halides using sodium metal in dry ether.

Primary and secondary alkyl halides readily undergo Wurtz reaction to form alkanes.

Tertiary alkyl halides, due to high steric hindrance, undergo dehydrohalogenation (elimination) rather than coupling when treated with sodium in dry ether, resulting in the formation of alkenes instead of alkanes.

Among the given options, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCl}$ is a tertiary alkyl halide, so it does not undergo Wurtz reaction.

Answer: $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCl}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following factors proceeds more rapidly, unimolecular nucleophilic substitution reaction?
questions.solution:
Unimolecular nucleophilic substitution ($S_{N}1$) reactions proceed via the formation of a carbocation intermediate in the rate-determining step.

Polar protic solvents have high dielectric constants and are capable of hydrogen bonding. They stabilize both the carbocation intermediate and the leaving group anion through solvation. This stabilization lowers the activation energy required for the cleavage of the carbon-halogen bond, thereby increasing the rate of the $S_{N}1$ reaction.

The strength of the nucleophile does not affect the rate of an $S_{N}1$ reaction because the nucleophile is not involved in the rate-determining step. Aprotic solvents generally favor $S_{N}2$ reactions.

Answer: Polar protic solvent

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds is carcinogenic and toxic?
questions.solution:
Benzene is a known human carcinogen and is highly toxic. Prolonged exposure to benzene can lead to severe health issues, including leukemia and other blood-related diseases.

Alkanes, alkenes, and alkynes in their simple forms are generally not considered carcinogenic.

Answer: Benzene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following is obtained as major product when methoxybenzene is treated with nitrating mixture?
questions.solution:
Methoxybenzene (anisole) undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution when treated with a nitrating mixture (conc. $\text{HNO}_3$ and conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$).

The $-\text{OCH}_3$ group is an electron-donating group through the $+R$ effect, which increases the electron density at the ortho and para positions of the benzene ring. Thus, it acts as an ortho, para-directing group.

Nitration of methoxybenzene yields a mixture of 2-nitroanisole (ortho product) and 4-nitroanisole (para product).

Due to steric hindrance at the ortho position caused by the bulky methoxy group, the para product, 4-nitroanisole, is formed as the major product.

Answer: 4-Nitroanisole

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is obtained when dihydrogen reacts with the alkali metals at high temperature?
questions.solution:
Alkali metals react with dihydrogen at high temperatures to form the corresponding metal hydrides.

$2M + H_2 \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2M^{+}H^{-}$

where $M$ represents an alkali metal (Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs). These hydrides are ionic (salt-like) in nature.

Answer: Metal hydrides

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
What happens when $\text{CuSO}_4$ is dissolved in water?
Identify correct statements from the following
options: Anion of the salt react with water.
Its solution will turn red litmus into blue.
The pH of the solution will be less than $7$.
The $\text{CuSO}_4$ will not undergo hydrolysis reaction.
questions.solution:
$\text{CuSO}_4$ is a salt of a weak base ($\text{Cu(OH)}_2$) and a strong acid ($\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$).

When dissolved in water, the $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ cation undergoes hydrolysis to produce $\text{H}^+$ ions:

$\text{Cu}^{2+} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{Cu(OH)}_2 + 2\text{H}^+$

Due to the generation of $\text{H}^+$ ions, the solution becomes acidic.

Therefore, the pH of the solution will be less than $7$.

The anion $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ does not undergo hydrolysis as it is derived from a strong acid.

An acidic solution turns blue litmus red, not red litmus blue.

Answer: The pH of the solution will be less than $7$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What happens when solid $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ dissolved in water?
questions.solution:
$\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ is a salt of a strong base ($\text{NaOH}$) and a weak acid ($\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3$).

When dissolved in water, it dissociates completely into $\text{Na}^+$ and $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$ ions.

The carbonate ion undergoes anionic hydrolysis:

$\text{CO}_3^{2-} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{HCO}_3^- + \text{OH}^-$

This hydrolysis produces $\text{OH}^-$ ions, leading to an increase in $[\text{OH}^-]$ concentration and making the solution basic.

Answer: an increase in $[\text{OH}^-]$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following aqueous solution of salt have $pH \lt  7$ at $298$ K?
questions.solution:
$\text{KNO}_3$ is a salt of a strong acid ($\text{HNO}_3$) and a strong base ($\text{KOH}$). Its aqueous solution does not undergo hydrolysis and remains neutral with $\text{pH} = 7$.

$\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ is a salt of a weak acid ($\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3$) and a strong base ($\text{NaOH}$). It undergoes anionic hydrolysis, making the solution basic with $\text{pH} \gt 7$.

$\text{CH}_3\text{COONH}_4$ is a salt of a weak acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$) and a weak base ($\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$). Since $K_a \approx K_b$, its aqueous solution is almost neutral with $\text{pH} \approx 7$.

$\text{CuCl}_2$ is a salt of a strong acid ($\text{HCl}$) and a weak base ($\text{Cu(OH)}_2$). The $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ ion undergoes cationic hydrolysis to produce $\text{H}^+$ ions, making the solution acidic with $\text{pH} \lt 7$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is not characteristics of interhalogen compounds?
options: Form addition products with unsaturated hydrocarbons.
questions.solution:
Interhalogen compounds are formed by the combination of two different halogens. They are covalent in nature due to the small electronegativity difference between the halogen atoms.

They are generally volatile solids or liquids (except $ClF$, which is a gas) and are not explosive.

They are highly reactive and form addition products with unsaturated hydrocarbons.

Because halogens are highly electronegative, interhalogen compounds have a strong tendency to accept electrons. Therefore, they act as strong oxidizing agents, not reducing agents.

Answer: Behave as strong reducing agent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following polymers is also called as dacron?
questions.solution:
Dacron is the trade name for the polymer polyethylene terephthalate (PET) in the United States, while in the United Kingdom, it is commonly known as Terylene.

It is a polyester made by the condensation polymerization of ethylene glycol and terephthalic acid.

Therefore, Terylene is also called Dacron.

Answer: Terylene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds are used to obtain terylene polymer?
questions.solution:
Terylene, also known as Dacron, is a polyester.

It is prepared by the condensation polymerization of ethylene glycol and terephthalic acid.

The IUPAC name of ethylene glycol is ethane-1,2-diol.

The IUPAC name of terephthalic acid is benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid.

Therefore, the monomers used to obtain terylene are ethane-1,2-diol and benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid.

Answer: Ethane-1,2-diol and Benzene-1, 4 dicarboxylic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the total number of spheres that surrounds the tetrahedral hole in the close-packed three-dimensional structure?
questions.solution:
A tetrahedral void is formed when a sphere of the second layer is placed exactly over the triangular void formed by three spheres of the first layer.

Thus, a tetrahedral hole is surrounded by $4$ spheres ($3$ in one layer and $1$ in the adjacent layer).

The coordination number of a tetrahedral void is $4$.

Answer: $4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
In a cubic unit cell of an ionic compound, the eight corners are occupied by anions and cations at the center of the cube. Calculate the volume of the unit cell if density of the unit cell is $4 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$.
[Molar mass of compound $= 168.6$ g mol$^{-1}$ and $N_A = 6.022 \times 10^{23}$]
questions.solution:
Number of anions per unit cell $= 8 \times \dfrac{1}{8} = 1$

Number of cations per unit cell $= 1$

Total number of formula units per unit cell, $Z = 1$

The density of the unit cell is given by the formula:

$d = \dfrac{Z \times M}{N_A \times V}$

Rearranging for volume $V$:

$V = \dfrac{Z \times M}{N_A \times d}$

Substituting the given values:

$V = \dfrac{1 \times 168.6}{6.022 \times 10^{23} \times 4}$

$V = \dfrac{168.6}{24.088 \times 10^{23}}$

$V = 7.0 \times 10^{-23} \text{ cm}^3$

Answer: $7.0 \times 10^{-23} \text{ cm}^3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Pt has FCC structure with an edge length of unit cell $392$ pm. What is the radius of Pt?
questions.solution:
For an FCC (face-centered cubic) structure, the relationship between the edge length $a$ and the atomic radius $r$ is given by:

$4r = \sqrt{2}a$

$r = \dfrac{a}{2\sqrt{2}}$

Given $a = 392$ pm:

$r = \dfrac{392}{2\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{196}{\sqrt{2}}$

$r = 98\sqrt{2}$

Using $\sqrt{2} \approx 1.414$:

$r = 98 \times 1.414 = 138.57$ pm $\approx 138.6$ pm

Answer: $138.6$ pm

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify from the following pair of solutions that exhibits the same osmotic pressure.
[molar mass of urea $= 60$ g mol$^{-1}$ and molar mass of glucose $= 180$ g mol$^{-1}$]
options: $6$ g/L urea solution and $18$ g/L glucose solution.
$12$ g/L urea solution and $18$ g/L glucose solution.
$18$ g/L urea solution and $18$ g/L glucose solution.
$6$ g/L urea solution and $6$ g/L glucose solution.
questions.solution:
Osmotic pressure is given by $\pi = iCRT$.

For non-electrolytes like urea and glucose, the van't Hoff factor $i = 1$.

For two solutions to exhibit the same osmotic pressure at a given temperature, their molar concentrations must be equal ($C_1 = C_2$).

Molar concentration $C = \dfrac{\text{mass per unit volume}}{\text{molar mass}}$.

For $6$ g/L urea solution:
$C_{\text{urea}} = \dfrac{6}{60} = 0.1$ mol/L

For $18$ g/L glucose solution:
$C_{\text{glucose}} = \dfrac{18}{180} = 0.1$ mol/L

Since $C_{\text{urea}} = C_{\text{glucose}}$, these two solutions are isotonic and exhibit the same osmotic pressure.

Answer: $6$ g/L urea solution and $18$ g/L glucose solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The solubility of $\text{N}_2$ gas in water at $25^\circ$C and $1$ bar is $6.85 \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol L}^{-1}$. Calculate the solubility of $\text{N}_2$ gas in water at the same temperature when the partial pressure of $\text{N}_2$ is $0.70$ bar
questions.solution:
According to Henry's law, the solubility of a gas in a liquid is directly proportional to its partial pressure at a constant temperature.

$S \propto P$

$\dfrac{S_1}{P_1} = \dfrac{S_2}{P_2}$

Given $S_1 = 6.85 \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol L}^{-1}$, $P_1 = 1 \text{ bar}$, and $P_2 = 0.70 \text{ bar}$.

$S_2 = S_1 \times \dfrac{P_2}{P_1}$

$S_2 = 6.85 \times 10^{-4} \times \dfrac{0.70}{1}$

$S_2 = 4.795 \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol L}^{-1}$

Answer: $4.795 \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol L}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Vapour pressure of $\text{CCl}_4$ at $25^\circ$C is $143$ mm Hg. If $0.5$ g of a non-volatile solute is dissolved in $100 \text{ cm}^3$ of $\text{CCl}_4$. Find the vapour pressure of the solution.
(Density of $\text{CCl}_4 = 1.58 \text{ g}/\text{cm}^3$ and molecular weight of solute is $65$)
questions.solution:
Mass of solvent ($CCl_4$), $W_1 = \text{Volume} \times \text{Density} = 100 \times 1.58 = 158 \text{ g}$

Molar mass of $CCl_4$, $M_1 = 12 + 4(35.5) = 154 \text{ g/mol}$

Number of moles of solvent, $n_1 = \dfrac{W_1}{M_1} = \dfrac{158}{154} \approx 1.026$

Mass of solute, $W_2 = 0.5 \text{ g}$

Molar mass of solute, $M_2 = 65 \text{ g/mol}$

Number of moles of solute, $n_2 = \dfrac{W_2}{M_2} = \dfrac{0.5}{65} \approx 0.0077$

According to Raoult's law, the relative lowering of vapour pressure is given by:

$\dfrac{P^0 - P_s}{P^0} = \dfrac{n_2}{n_1 + n_2}$

$\dfrac{143 - P_s}{143} = \dfrac{0.0077}{1.026 + 0.0077}$

$\dfrac{143 - P_s}{143} = \dfrac{0.0077}{1.0337} \approx 0.00745$

$143 - P_s = 143 \times 0.00745 \approx 1.065$

$P_s = 143 - 1.065 = 141.935 \text{ mm Hg}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the mass of $100$ molecules of oxygen in amu and in grams.
questions.solution:
Mass of one oxygen molecule ($O_2$) = $2 \times 16$ u = $32$ u.

Mass of $100$ oxygen molecules = $100 \times 32$ u = $3200$ u.

Since $1$ u = $1.6605 \times 10^{-24}$ g, the mass in grams is given by:

Mass = $3200 \times 1.6605 \times 10^{-24}$ g = $5.314 \times 10^{-21}$ g.

Answer: $3200$ u and $5.314 \times 10^{-21}$ g

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: According to the kinetic molecular theory of gases, the average kinetic energy of gas molecules:
options: Is directly proportional to the absolute temperature
Is the same for all gases at the same volume
questions.solution:
According to the kinetic molecular theory of gases, the average translational kinetic energy of a gas molecule is given by $E = \dfrac{3}{2}kT$, where $k$ is the Boltzmann constant and $T$ is the absolute temperature.

For one mole of an ideal gas, the average kinetic energy is $E = \dfrac{3}{2}RT$, where $R$ is the universal gas constant.

This shows that the average kinetic energy of gas molecules depends only on the absolute temperature and is directly proportional to it. It is independent of pressure, volume, and the nature of the gas.

Answer: Is directly proportional to the absolute temperature

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List I with List II
List I
Element		List II
Number of Neutron
(A). ${}^{24}_{12}Mg$(I). $5$
(B). ${}^{27}_{13}Al$(II). $12$
(C). ${}^{9}_{4}Be$(III). $6$
(D). ${}^{12}_{6}C$(IV). $14$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The number of neutrons in an atom is calculated as the difference between its mass number ($A$) and atomic number ($Z$), i.e., $n = A - Z$.

For ${}^{24}_{12}Mg$, $n = 24 - 12 = 12$. This matches (II).

For ${}^{27}_{13}Al$, $n = 27 - 13 = 14$. This matches (IV).

For ${}^{9}_{4}Be$, $n = 9 - 4 = 5$. This matches (I).

For ${}^{12}_{6}C$, $n = 12 - 6 = 6$. This matches (III).

The correct matching is (A) - (II), (B) - (IV), (C) - (I), (D) - (III).

Answer: (A) - (II), (B) - (IV), (C) - (I), (D) - (III)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following assertions about the extent of physisorption is correct?
options: Decreases with increase in surface area
Decreases with increase in the strength of Van der Waals forces
questions.solution:
Physisorption is an exothermic process. According to Le Chatelier's principle, an increase in temperature shifts the equilibrium in the backward direction, leading to desorption. Thus, the extent of physisorption decreases with an increase in temperature.

Additionally, the extent of physisorption increases with an increase in the surface area of the adsorbent and with an increase in the strength of Van der Waals forces between the adsorbate and adsorbent.

Answer: Decreases with increase in temperature

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following processes exhibits, $\Delta U = 0$?
questions.solution:
The internal energy of an ideal gas is a function of temperature only.

The change in internal energy is given by $\Delta U = n C_v \Delta T$.

In an isothermal process, the temperature of the system remains constant, which implies $\Delta T = 0$.

Substituting $\Delta T = 0$ yields $\Delta U = 0$.

Therefore, an isothermal process exhibits $\Delta U = 0$.

Answer: Isothermal process

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the work done when $1$ mole of an ideal gas is expanded reversibly and isothermally from initial pressure $10$ bar to final pressure $1$ bar at constant temperature $300$ K. [$R = 8.314 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$]
questions.solution:
For a reversible isothermal expansion of an ideal gas, the work done is given by the formula:

$W = -2.303 nRT \log_{10}\left(\dfrac{P_1}{P_2}\right)$

Given:
$n = 1 \text{ mol}$
$R = 8.314 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$
$T = 300 \text{ K}$
$P_1 = 10 \text{ bar}$
$P_2 = 1 \text{ bar}$

Substituting the values into the formula:

$W = -2.303 \times 1 \times 8.314 \times 300 \times \log_{10}\left(\dfrac{10}{1}\right)$

$W = -2.303 \times 2494.2 \times 1$

$W = -5744.14 \text{ J}$

$W = -5.744 \text{ kJ}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Calculate the enthalpy change for the following reaction, using given bond energy (kJ/mol)
(C-H = $414$, H-O = $463$, H-Cl = $431$, C-Cl = $326$ and C-O = $335$)
$\text{CH}_3\text{OH}_{(g)} + \text{HCl}_{(g)} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{Cl}_{(g)} + \text{H}_2\text{O}_{(g)}$
questions.solution:
The enthalpy of reaction is given by:

$\Delta H = \sum \text{BE(Reactants)} - \sum \text{BE(Products)}$

$\Delta H = [3 \times \text{BE(C-H)} + \text{BE(C-O)} + \text{BE(O-H)} + \text{BE(H-Cl)}] - [3 \times \text{BE(C-H)} + \text{BE(C-Cl)} + 2 \times \text{BE(O-H)}]$

Canceling the common bond energies on both sides:

$\Delta H = \text{BE(C-O)} + \text{BE(H-Cl)} - \text{BE(C-Cl)} - \text{BE(O-H)}$

Substituting the given values:

$\Delta H = 335 + 431 - 326 - 463$

$\Delta H = 766 - 789 = -23 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $-23 \text{ kJmol}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The equation of the tangent to the curve $y = 3x^3 - 3x^2 + x$ at $x = 1$ is
questions.solution:
Given curve is $y = 3x^3 - 3x^2 + x$

Substituting $x = 1$, we get $y = 3(1)^3 - 3(1)^2 + 1 = 1$

The point of tangency is $(1, 1)$

Differentiating the given equation with respect to $x$, we get

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 9x^2 - 6x + 1$

The slope of the tangent at $x = 1$ is

$m = \left( \dfrac{dy}{dx} \right)_{x=1} = 9(1)^2 - 6(1) + 1 = 4$

The equation of the tangent at $(1, 1)$ is

$y - 1 = 4(x - 1)$

$y - 1 = 4x - 4$

$4x - y - 3 = 0$

Answer: $4x - y - 3 = 0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The approximate value of $\sqrt[3]{63}$ is
questions.solution:
Let $f(x) = x^{1/3}$.

Let $x = 64$ and $\Delta x = -1$.

We know that $f(x + \Delta x) \approx f(x) + f'(x) \Delta x$.

Differentiating $f(x)$ with respect to $x$, we get:

$f'(x) = \dfrac{1}{3} x^{-2/3}$

At $x = 64$, $f'(64) = \dfrac{1}{3} (64)^{-2/3} = \dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{1}{16} = \dfrac{1}{48}$

Now, $\Delta y \approx f'(64) \Delta x = \dfrac{1}{48} \times (-1) \approx -0.02083$

Therefore, the approximate value is:

$f(63) \approx 4 - 0.02083 = 3.97917$

A more precise calculation using the binomial expansion yields $3.979057$, which rounds to $3.9791$. The closest given option is $3.9791$.

Answer: $3.9791$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A wire of length $64$ m is to be bent to form a rectangle such that its area is maximum, then its area is.....
questions.solution:
Let the length and breadth of the rectangle be $x$ and $y$ respectively.

The perimeter of the rectangle is equal to the length of the wire.

$2(x + y) = 64$

$x + y = 32$

The area of the rectangle is $A = xy$.

Using the AM-GM inequality for positive numbers $x$ and $y$:

$\dfrac{x + y}{2} \ge \sqrt{xy}$

$\dfrac{32}{2} \ge \sqrt{A}$

$16 \ge \sqrt{A}$

$A \le 256$

The maximum area of the rectangle is $256$ sq.m, which occurs when $x = y = 16$ m (when the rectangle is a square).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The difference between the local extreme values of the function $f(x) = 2x^3 - 15x^2 + 36x + 40$ is ......
questions.solution:
Given $f(x) = 2x^3 - 15x^2 + 36x + 40$

Differentiating with respect to $x$:

$f'(x) = 6x^2 - 30x + 36$

For local extrema, $f'(x) = 0$:

$6(x^2 - 5x + 6) = 0$

$(x - 2)(x - 3) = 0$

$x = 2, 3$

Evaluating the function at the critical points:

$f(2) = 2(2)^3 - 15(2)^2 + 36(2) + 40 = 16 - 60 + 72 + 40 = 68$

$f(3) = 2(3)^3 - 15(3)^2 + 36(3) + 40 = 54 - 135 + 108 + 40 = 67$

The difference between the local extreme values is $68 - 67 = 1$.

Answer: $1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int_0^3 \sqrt{9 - x^2} dx = $
questions.solution:
Using the standard integral formula:

$\int \sqrt{a^2 - x^2} dx = \dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{a^2 - x^2} + \dfrac{a^2}{2}\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right)$

Applying the limits from $0$ to $3$ with $a = 3$:

$\int_0^3 \sqrt{9 - x^2} dx = \left[ \dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{9 - x^2} + \dfrac{9}{2}\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) \right]_0^3$

$= \left( 0 + \dfrac{9}{2}\sin^{-1}(1) \right) - \left( 0 + \dfrac{9}{2}\sin^{-1}(0) \right)$

$= \dfrac{9}{2} \times \dfrac{\pi}{2} - 0$

$= \dfrac{9\pi}{4}$

Alternatively, the integral represents the area of a quarter circle of radius $3$ in the first quadrant, which is $\dfrac{1}{4} \times \pi(3)^2 = \dfrac{9\pi}{4}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of the shaded region is ... sq.units.
questions.solution:
From the given figure, the shaded region is bounded by the curve $y = \sin x$ from $x = 2\pi$ to $x = \dfrac{9\pi}{4}$ and by the curve $y = \cos x$ from $x = \dfrac{9\pi}{4}$ to $x = \dfrac{5\pi}{2}$.

The area $A$ of the shaded region is given by the sum of two definite integrals:

$A = \int_{2\pi}^{\dfrac{9\pi}{4}} \sin x \, dx + \int_{\dfrac{9\pi}{4}}^{\dfrac{5\pi}{2}} \cos x \, dx$

Evaluating the first integral:

$\int_{2\pi}^{\dfrac{9\pi}{4}} \sin x \, dx = [-\cos x]_{2\pi}^{\dfrac{9\pi}{4}} = -\cos\left(\dfrac{9\pi}{4}\right) - (-\cos(2\pi))$

$= -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} - (-1) = 1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Evaluating the second integral:

$\int_{\dfrac{9\pi}{4}}^{\dfrac{5\pi}{2}} \cos x \, dx = [\sin x]_{\dfrac{9\pi}{4}}^{\dfrac{5\pi}{2}} = \sin\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{2}\right) - \sin\left(\dfrac{9\pi}{4}\right)$

$= 1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Adding the two areas:

$A = \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) + \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = 2 - \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2}} = 2 - \sqrt{2}$

Answer: $2 - \sqrt{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $A = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}$, then which of the following statements is not true?
questions.solution:
Given the set $A = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}$.

Checking the first statement: $\exists x \in A$, such that $x + 4 \leq 9$. For $x = 1$, $1 + 4 = 5 \leq 9$. This statement is true.

Checking the second statement: $\exists x \in A$, such that $12 - x = 7$. Solving for $x$ gives $x = 5$. Since $5 \in A$, this statement is true.

Checking the third statement: $\forall x \in A, x + 3 \geq 4$. The minimum value of $x$ in $A$ is $1$. For $x = 1$, $1 + 3 = 4 \geq 4$. For all other values in $A$, $x + 3 \gt 4$. This statement is true.

Checking the fourth statement: $\exists x \in A$, such that $x + 2 \lt 3$. Solving for $x$ gives $x \lt 1$. There is no element in $A$ that is strictly less than $1$. This statement is false.

Therefore, the fourth statement is not true.

Answer: $\exists x \in A$, such that $x + 2 \lt 3$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The equation of a circle which passes through the points $(2,3)$ and $(4,5)$ and whose center lies on the straight line $y - 4x + 3 = 0$ is
questions.solution:
Let the center of the circle be $(h, k)$.

Since the center lies on the line $y - 4x + 3 = 0$, we have:
$k - 4h + 3 = 0 \Rightarrow k = 4h - 3$

The circle passes through $(2,3)$ and $(4,5)$, so the distance from the center to both points is equal to the radius $r$.
$(h - 2)^2 + (k - 3)^2 = (h - 4)^2 + (k - 5)^2$

Expanding both sides:
$h^2 - 4h + 4 + k^2 - 6k + 9 = h^2 - 8h + 16 + k^2 - 10k + 25$

Simplifying the equation:
$4h + 4k = 28 \Rightarrow h + k = 7$

Substituting $k = 4h - 3$ into the above equation:
$h + 4h - 3 = 7 \Rightarrow 5h = 10 \Rightarrow h = 2$

Then, $k = 4(2) - 3 = 5$.
The center of the circle is $(2, 5)$.

The radius squared is:
$r^2 = (2 - 2)^2 + (5 - 3)^2 = 4$

The equation of the circle is:
$(x - 2)^2 + (y - 5)^2 = 4$
$x^2 - 4x + 4 + y^2 - 10y + 25 = 4$
$x^2 + y^2 - 4x - 10y + 25 = 0$

Answer: $x^2 + y^2 - 4x - 10y + 25 = 0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $-1 + \sqrt{-3} = r e^{i\theta}$, then the value of $\theta$ is
questions.solution:
Given complex number is $z = -1 + \sqrt{-3} = -1 + i\sqrt{3}$.

Let $z = r e^{i\theta}$, where $r = |z|$ and $\theta = \arg(z)$.

The real part $x = -1$ and the imaginary part $y = \sqrt{3}$.

Since $x \lt 0$ and $y \gt 0$, the complex number lies in the second quadrant.

The principal argument $\theta$ is given by $\pi - \tan^{-1}\left(\left|\dfrac{y}{x}\right|\right)$.

$\theta = \pi - \tan^{-1}(\sqrt{3}) = \pi - \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Let the function $f(x)$ be defined as:
$f(x) = \begin{cases} \left[\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + x\right)\right]^{\dfrac{1}{x}}, & x \neq 0 \\ k, & x = 0 \end{cases}$
If $f(x)$ is continuous at $x = 0$, then the value of $k$ is...
questions.solution:
For $f(x)$ to be continuous at $x = 0$, we must have $f(0) = \lim_{x \to 0} f(x)$.

$k = \lim_{x \to 0} \left[\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + x\right)\right]^{\dfrac{1}{x}}$

This limit is of the form $1^{\infty}$. Using the standard limit $\lim_{x \to a} f(x)^{g(x)} = e^{\lim_{x \to a} g(x)(f(x) - 1)}$, we get:

$k = e^{\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{1}{x} \left[ \tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + x\right) - 1 \right]}$

Using the identity $\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + x\right) = \dfrac{1 + \tan x}{1 - \tan x}$, we have:

$\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + x\right) - 1 = \dfrac{1 + \tan x}{1 - \tan x} - 1 = \dfrac{2\tan x}{1 - \tan x}$

Substituting this back into the limit:

$k = e^{\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{1}{x} \left( \dfrac{2\tan x}{1 - \tan x} \right)}$

$k = e^{\lim_{x \to 0} \left( \dfrac{\tan x}{x} \right) \left( \dfrac{2}{1 - \tan x} \right)}$

Since $\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{\tan x}{x} = 1$ and $\lim_{x \to 0} \tan x = 0$, we get:

$k = e^{1 \times \dfrac{2}{1 - 0}} = e^2$

Answer: $e^2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\int_1^a (2x + 1) dx = 5$, then the sum of the values of $a$ is..
questions.solution:
Evaluating the definite integral:

$\int_1^a (2x + 1) dx = [x^2 + x]_1^a$

Substituting the limits:

$(a^2 + a) - (1^2 + 1) = 5$

$a^2 + a - 2 = 5$

$a^2 + a - 7 = 0$

This is a quadratic equation in $a$. The sum of the roots of the equation is $-\dfrac{1}{1} = -1$.

Answer: $-1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $[\cdot]$ denotes the greatest integer function, then $\int_1^4 x[x] dx$ is equal to
questions.solution:
The given integral can be split at integer values since $[x]$ changes its value at integers.

$I = \int_1^4 x[x] dx$

$I = \int_1^2 x[x] dx + \int_2^3 x[x] dx + \int_3^4 x[x] dx$

Substituting the values of $[x]$ in the respective intervals:

$I = \int_1^2 x(1) dx + \int_2^3 x(2) dx + \int_3^4 x(3) dx$

$I = \left[ \dfrac{x^2}{2} \right]_1^2 + \left[ x^2 \right]_2^3 + \left[ \dfrac{3x^2}{2} \right]_3^4$

$I = \left( \dfrac{4}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2} \right) + (9 - 4) + \left( \dfrac{48}{2} - \dfrac{27}{2} \right)$

$I = \dfrac{3}{2} + 5 + \dfrac{21}{2}$

$I = \dfrac{24}{2} + 5$

$I = 12 + 5 = 17$

Answer: $17$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The order and degree of the differential equation $\sqrt{2 + \left(\dfrac{d^2 y}{dx^2}\right)^3} = \left(\dfrac{d^3 y}{dx^3}\right)^{5/2}$ respectively are
questions.solution:
The given differential equation is $\sqrt{2 + \left(\dfrac{d^2 y}{dx^2}\right)^3} = \left(\dfrac{d^3 y}{dx^3}\right)^{5/2}$

Squaring both sides to remove fractional powers, we get:

$2 + \left(\dfrac{d^2 y}{dx^2}\right)^3 = \left(\dfrac{d^3 y}{dx^3}\right)^5$

The highest order derivative present in the equation is $\dfrac{d^3 y}{dx^3}$, so the order of the differential equation is $3$.

The power of the highest order derivative is $5$, so the degree of the differential equation is $5$.

Therefore, the order and degree are $3$ and $5$ respectively.

Answer: $3, 5$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The differential equation representing the family of curves $x \sin x + y^3 = 4ax$ is
questions.solution:
The given equation of the family of curves is $x \sin x + y^3 = 4ax$.

Dividing the entire equation by $x$, we get:

$\sin x + \dfrac{y^3}{x} = 4a$

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain:

$\cos x + \dfrac{3y^2 \dfrac{dy}{dx} \cdot x - y^3 \cdot 1}{x^2} = 0$

Multiplying the equation by $x^2$ gives:

$x^2 \cos x + 3xy^2 \dfrac{dy}{dx} - y^3 = 0$

Rearranging the terms to solve for $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$:

$3xy^2 \dfrac{dy}{dx} = y^3 - x^2 \cos x$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y^3 - x^2 \cos x}{3xy^2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y^3 - x^2 \cos x}{3xy^2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The particular solution of the differential equation $xdy + 2ydx = 0$, when $x = 2$ and $y = 1$ is
questions.solution:
The given differential equation is $xdy + 2ydx = 0$

Separating the variables, we get:

$\dfrac{dy}{y} + \dfrac{2dx}{x} = 0$

Integrating both sides:

$\int \dfrac{dy}{y} + 2 \int \dfrac{dx}{x} = 0$

$\ln y + 2 \ln x = \ln C$

$\ln(y x^2) = \ln C$

$x^2 y = C$

Substituting $x = 2$ and $y = 1$:

$(2)^2(1) = C \Rightarrow C = 4$

The particular solution is $x^2 y = 4$

Taking the square root on both sides:

$x\sqrt{y} = \pm 2$

Since $x = 2$ and $y = 1$ satisfies the positive root, we get:

$x\sqrt{y} = 2$

Answer: $x\sqrt{y} = 2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $y = \sin(e^{\log 2x})$, then the value of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ at $x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ is
questions.solution:
Given $y = \sin(e^{\log 2x})$

Using the property $e^{\log a} = a$, we get $e^{\log 2x} = 2x$

Therefore, $y = \sin(2x)$

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2\cos(2x)$

Substituting $x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2\cos\left(2 \times \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = 2\cos(\pi)$

Since $\cos(\pi) = -1$, we have:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2(-1) = -2$

Answer: $-2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $y = \sqrt{x + \sqrt{x^2 + 1}}$, then the value of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is
questions.solution:
Given $y = \sqrt{x + \sqrt{x^2 + 1}}$

Squaring both sides:

$y^2 = x + \sqrt{x^2 + 1}$

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$:

$2y \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1 + \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x^2 + 1}} \cdot 2x$

$2y \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1 + \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{x^2 + 1}}$

$2y \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\sqrt{x^2 + 1} + x}{\sqrt{x^2 + 1}}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\sqrt{x^2 + 1} + x}{2y\sqrt{x^2 + 1}}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\sqrt{x^2 + 1} + x}{2y\sqrt{x^2 + 1}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $y = \sqrt{\tan x + \sqrt{\tan x + \sqrt{\tan x + \cdots \cdots \cdots \infty}}}$, then $\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2$ at $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ is
questions.solution:
Given $y = \sqrt{\tan x + \sqrt{\tan x + \sqrt{\tan x + \cdots \infty}}}$

Squaring both sides, we get:

$y^2 = \tan x + y$

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$:

$2y \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \sec^2 x + \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} (2y - 1) = \sec^2 x$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\sec^2 x}{2y - 1}$

At $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$, $\tan x = 1$. Substituting this into the equation for $y$:

$y^2 - y - 1 = 0$

Solving for $y$, we get $y = \dfrac{1 \pm \sqrt{5}}{2}$. Since $y$ represents a principal square root, $y \gt 0$, so $y = \dfrac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}$.

Substituting $y = \dfrac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}$ and $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ into the derivative:

$2y - 1 = 2\left(\dfrac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}\right) - 1 = \sqrt{5}$

$\sec^2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = (\sqrt{2})^2 = 2$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{5}}$

Squaring both sides:

$\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 = \dfrac{4}{5}$

Answer: $\dfrac{4}{5}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $y = \sqrt{x^2 + 8x + 3}$, then the value of $\dfrac{d^2 y}{dx^2}$ at $x = 3$ is
questions.solution:
Given $y = \sqrt{x^2 + 8x + 3}$

Squaring both sides:

$y^2 = x^2 + 8x + 3$

Differentiating with respect to $x$:

$2y \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2x + 8 \Rightarrow y \dfrac{dy}{dx} = x + 4$

Differentiating again with respect to $x$:

$y \dfrac{d^2 y}{dx^2} + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 = 1$

At $x = 3$, $y = \sqrt{3^2 + 8(3) + 3} = \sqrt{36} = 6$

Substituting $x = 3$ and $y = 6$ in the first derivative equation:

$6 \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 3 + 4 \Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{7}{6}$

Substituting $y = 6$ and $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{7}{6}$ in the second derivative equation:

$6 \dfrac{d^2 y}{dx^2} + \left(\dfrac{7}{6}\right)^2 = 1$

$6 \dfrac{d^2 y}{dx^2} = 1 - \dfrac{49}{36} = \dfrac{-13}{36}$

$\dfrac{d^2 y}{dx^2} = \dfrac{-13}{216}$

Answer: $\dfrac{-13}{216}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $y = f\left(\dfrac{3 + 2x}{3 - 2x}\right)$, where $f(x) = \tan(\log x)$ and $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \left(\dfrac{A}{B + C x^2}\right) \cdot \sec^2\left(\log\left(\dfrac{3 + 2x}{3 - 2x}\right)\right)$, then the respective values of A, B and C are ......
questions.solution:
Given $y = f\left(\dfrac{3 + 2x}{3 - 2x}\right)$ and $f(x) = \tan(\log x)$

$y = \tan\left(\log\left(\dfrac{3 + 2x}{3 - 2x}\right)\right)$

Differentiating with respect to $x$ using the chain rule:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \sec^2\left(\log\left(\dfrac{3 + 2x}{3 - 2x}\right)\right) \cdot \dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\log\left(\dfrac{3 + 2x}{3 - 2x}\right)\right)$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \sec^2\left(\log\left(\dfrac{3 + 2x}{3 - 2x}\right)\right) \cdot \dfrac{3 - 2x}{3 + 2x} \cdot \dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{3 + 2x}{3 - 2x}\right)$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \sec^2\left(\log\left(\dfrac{3 + 2x}{3 - 2x}\right)\right) \cdot \dfrac{3 - 2x}{3 + 2x} \cdot \left(\dfrac{2(3 - 2x) - (-2)(3 + 2x)}{(3 - 2x)^2}\right)$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \sec^2\left(\log\left(\dfrac{3 + 2x}{3 - 2x}\right)\right) \cdot \dfrac{3 - 2x}{3 + 2x} \cdot \dfrac{12}{(3 - 2x)^2}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{12}{(3 + 2x)(3 - 2x)} \cdot \sec^2\left(\log\left(\dfrac{3 + 2x}{3 - 2x}\right)\right)$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{12}{9 - 4x^2} \cdot \sec^2\left(\log\left(\dfrac{3 + 2x}{3 - 2x}\right)\right)$

Comparing with the given expression $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \left(\dfrac{A}{B + C x^2}\right) \cdot \sec^2\left(\log\left(\dfrac{3 + 2x}{3 - 2x}\right)\right)$

We get $A = 12$, $B = 9$, $C = -4$.

Answer: $12, 9, -4$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The domain of the function $f(x) = \sqrt{x - 1} + \sqrt{3 - x}$ is ...
questions.solution:
For the function $f(x) = \sqrt{x - 1} + \sqrt{3 - x}$ to be defined, the expressions inside the square roots must be non-negative.

$x - 1 \ge 0 \Rightarrow x \ge 1$

$3 - x \ge 0 \Rightarrow x \le 3$

Taking the intersection of both conditions, we get $1 \le x \le 3$.

Thus, the domain of the function is $[1, 3]$.

Answer: $[1, 3]$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int \dfrac{x}{x + 2} dx$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $I = \int \dfrac{x}{x + 2} dx$

Adding and subtracting $2$ in the numerator, we get:

$I = \int \dfrac{x + 2 - 2}{x + 2} dx$

$I = \int \left(1 - \dfrac{2}{x + 2}\right) dx$

Integrating with respect to $x$:

$I = x - 2\log(x + 2) + c$

Answer: $x - 2\log(x + 2) + c$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\int \dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{2ax - x^2}} = f(g(x)) + c$, where $c$ is constant of integration, then $f(x), g(x)$ are respectively equal to
questions.solution:
The given integral is $I = \int \dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{2ax - x^2}}$

Completing the square for the expression inside the square root:

$2ax - x^2 = a^2 - (x^2 - 2ax + a^2) = a^2 - (x - a)^2$

Substituting this back into the integral:

$I = \int \dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{a^2 - (x - a)^2}}$

Using the standard integration formula $\int \dfrac{dt}{\sqrt{a^2 - t^2}} = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{t}{a}\right) + c$, we get:

$I = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x - a}{a}\right) + c$

Comparing this with $f(g(x)) + c$, we have:

$f(x) = \sin^{-1} x$

$g(x) = \dfrac{x - a}{a}$

Answer: $\sin^{-1} x, \dfrac{x - a}{a}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int \dfrac{x + 2}{x^2 - 7x + 12} dx$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $I = \int \dfrac{x + 2}{x^2 - 7x + 12} dx$

Factorizing the denominator, we get $x^2 - 7x + 12 = (x - 3)(x - 4)$

Using partial fractions:

$\dfrac{x + 2}{(x - 3)(x - 4)} = \dfrac{A}{x - 3} + \dfrac{B}{x - 4}$

$x + 2 = A(x - 4) + B(x - 3)$

Substituting $x = 3$, we get $5 = -A \Rightarrow A = -5$

Substituting $x = 4$, we get $6 = B \Rightarrow B = 6$

Therefore, the integral becomes:

$I = \int \left( \dfrac{-5}{x - 3} + \dfrac{6}{x - 4} \right) dx$

$I = -5\log|x - 3| + 6\log|x - 4| + c$

Answer: $-5\log|x - 3| + 6\log|x - 4| + c$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\tan^{-1}(1) + \tan^{-1}(3) + \tan^{-1}(5) + \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right) = \pi + \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\right)$, then the value of $\alpha$ is...
questions.solution:
Grouping the terms of the left hand side:

$\tan^{-1}(1) + \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right) = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1 + \dfrac{1}{4}}{1 - \dfrac{1}{4}}\right) = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{5}{3}\right)$

Adding $\tan^{-1}(3)$ to this result:

$\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{5}{3}\right) + \tan^{-1}(3) = \pi + \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\dfrac{5}{3} + 3}{1 - \dfrac{5}{3} \times 3}\right)$

$= \pi + \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{14}{-12}\right) = \pi - \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{7}{6}\right)$

Adding $\tan^{-1}(5)$ to this result:

$\pi - \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{7}{6}\right) + \tan^{-1}(5) = \pi + \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{5 - \dfrac{7}{6}}{1 + 5 \times \dfrac{7}{6}}\right)$

$= \pi + \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\dfrac{23}{6}}{\dfrac{41}{6}}\right) = \pi + \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{23}{41}\right)$

Equating this to the right hand side:

$\pi + \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{23}{41}\right) = \pi + \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\right)$

$\dfrac{\alpha}{2} = \dfrac{23}{41} \Rightarrow \alpha = \dfrac{46}{41}$

Answer: $\dfrac{46}{41}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The minimum value of $(\sin^{-1} x)^2 + (\cos^{-1} x)^2$ is............
questions.solution:
Let $y = (\sin^{-1} x)^2 + (\cos^{-1} x)^2$

Using the identity $\sin^{-1} x + \cos^{-1} x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, we can write $\cos^{-1} x = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \sin^{-1} x$

Substituting this into the expression for $y$:

$y = (\sin^{-1} x)^2 + \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \sin^{-1} x\right)^2$

Let $t = \sin^{-1} x$, where $t \in \left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$

$y = t^2 + \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - t\right)^2$

$y = 2t^2 - \pi t + \dfrac{\pi^2}{4}$

$y = 2\left(t^2 - \dfrac{\pi}{2}t\right) + \dfrac{\pi^2}{4}$

$y = 2\left(t - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)^2 - 2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)^2 + \dfrac{\pi^2}{4}$

$y = 2\left(t - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)^2 + \dfrac{\pi^2}{8}$

The minimum value occurs when $t = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$, which lies in the interval $\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$

Therefore, the minimum value is $\dfrac{\pi^2}{8}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi^2}{8}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of $\lim_{x \to 3} \dfrac{[x] - 3}{x - 3}$, where $[\cdot]$ denotes the greatest integer function, is.....
questions.solution:
Evaluate the left-hand limit (LHL) and right-hand limit (RHL) at $x = 3$.

For LHL, let $x \to 3^{-}$. Then $[x] = 2$.

LHL $= \lim_{x \to 3^{-}} \dfrac{[x] - 3}{x - 3} = \lim_{x \to 3^{-}} \dfrac{2 - 3}{x - 3} = \lim_{x \to 3^{-}} \dfrac{-1}{x - 3} = \infty$

For RHL, let $x \to 3^{+}$. Then $[x] = 3$.

RHL $= \lim_{x \to 3^{+}} \dfrac{[x] - 3}{x - 3} = \lim_{x \to 3^{+}} \dfrac{3 - 3}{x - 3} = \lim_{x \to 3^{+}} 0 = 0$

Since LHL \neq RHL, the limit does not exist.

Answer: does not exist

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The point at which the maximum value of $x + y$ subject to constraints $x + 2y \leq 70$ and $2x + y \leq 95, x \geq 0, y \geq 0$ is.
questions.solution:
The objective function to be maximized is $Z = x + y$.

The given constraints are:
$x + 2y \leq 70$
$2x + y \leq 95$
$x \geq 0, y \geq 0$

The corner points of the feasible region are determined by the intersections of the boundary lines $x + 2y = 70$, $2x + y = 95$, and the coordinate axes.

Solving $x + 2y = 70$ and $2x + y = 95$:
Multiplying the second equation by $2$ gives $4x + 2y = 190$.
Subtracting the first equation from this gives $3x = 120 \Rightarrow x = 40$.
Substituting $x = 40$ into $x + 2y = 70$ gives $40 + 2y = 70 \Rightarrow 2y = 30 \Rightarrow y = 15$.
The intersection point is $(40, 15)$.

The corner points of the bounded feasible region are $(0, 0)$, $(47.5, 0)$, $(40, 15)$, and $(0, 35)$.

Evaluating $Z = x + y$ at each corner point:
At $(0, 0)$, $Z = 0 + 0 = 0$
At $(47.5, 0)$, $Z = 47.5 + 0 = 47.5$
At $(40, 15)$, $Z = 40 + 15 = 55$
At $(0, 35)$, $Z = 0 + 35 = 35$

The maximum value of $Z$ is $55$, which occurs at the point $(40, 15)$.

Answer: $(40, 15)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The statement pattern $(p \vee q) \rightarrow \sim r$ is logically equivalent to
questions.solution:
The given statement pattern is $(p \vee q) \rightarrow \sim r$.

Using the logical equivalence $A \rightarrow B \equiv \sim A \vee B$, the expression can be rewritten by taking $A = p \vee q$ and $B = \sim r$.

$(p \vee q) \rightarrow \sim r \equiv \sim(p \vee q) \vee \sim r$

Applying De Morgan's law, $\sim(p \vee q) \equiv \sim p \wedge \sim q$.

Substituting this into the expression yields:

$(\sim p \wedge \sim q) \vee \sim r$

Answer: $(\sim p \wedge \sim q) \vee \sim r$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the truth value of the compound statement $[(p \vee q) \wedge (q \rightarrow r) \wedge (\sim r)] \rightarrow (p \wedge q)$ is False then the truth values of $p \rightarrow q$ and $q \rightarrow p$ are respectively......
questions.solution:
The compound statement $X \rightarrow Y$ is False if and only if $X$ is True and $Y$ is False.

Here, $X = (p \vee q) \wedge (q \rightarrow r) \wedge (\sim r)$ and $Y = p \wedge q$.

Since $X$ is True, each of its components must be True:
1) $\sim r$ is True $\Rightarrow r$ is False.
2) $q \rightarrow r$ is True. Since $r$ is False, $q$ must be False.
3) $p \vee q$ is True. Since $q$ is False, $p$ must be True.

Checking $Y$: $p \wedge q = T \wedge F = F$, which satisfies the condition that $Y$ is False.

Thus, $p = T$ and $q = F$.

Now, we evaluate $p \rightarrow q$ and $q \rightarrow p$:
$p \rightarrow q = T \rightarrow F = F$
$q \rightarrow p = F \rightarrow T = T$

The truth values are $(F, T)$.

Answer: $(F, T)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} 2i & i^3 \\ i^2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$, then $A^{-1}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given $A = \begin{bmatrix} 2i & i^3 \\ i^2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$

Substituting $i^2 = -1$ and $i^3 = -i$, we get:

$A = \begin{bmatrix} 2i & -i \\ -1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$

The determinant of $A$ is:

$|A| = (2i)(1) - (-i)(-1) = 2i - i = i$

The adjugate of $A$ is:

$\text{adj}(A) = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & i \\ 1 & 2i \end{bmatrix}$

The inverse of $A$ is given by $A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{|A|} \text{adj}(A)$

$A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{i} \begin{bmatrix} 1 & i \\ 1 & 2i \end{bmatrix}$

Since $\dfrac{1}{i} = -i$, we have:

$A^{-1} = -i \begin{bmatrix} 1 & i \\ 1 & 2i \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -i & -i^2 \\ -i & -2i^2 \end{bmatrix}$

Substituting $i^2 = -1$:

$A^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} -i & 1 \\ -i & 2 \end{bmatrix}$

Answer: $\begin{bmatrix} -i & 1 \\ -i & 2 \end{bmatrix}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $A = \dfrac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix} -1 & -\sqrt{3} \\ \sqrt{3} & -1 \end{bmatrix}$ then $A^{-1} - A^2$ is not
questions.solution:
Given $A = \dfrac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix} -1 & -\sqrt{3} \\ \sqrt{3} & -1 \end{bmatrix}$

Calculating $A^2$:

$A^2 = \dfrac{1}{4}\begin{bmatrix} -1 & -\sqrt{3} \\ \sqrt{3} & -1 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} -1 & -\sqrt{3} \\ \sqrt{3} & -1 \end{bmatrix} = \dfrac{1}{4}\begin{bmatrix} 1-3 & \sqrt{3}+\sqrt{3} \\ -\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{3} & -3+1 \end{bmatrix} = \dfrac{1}{4}\begin{bmatrix} -2 & 2\sqrt{3} \\ -2\sqrt{3} & -2 \end{bmatrix} = \dfrac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix} -1 & \sqrt{3} \\ -\sqrt{3} & -1 \end{bmatrix}$

Now, finding the determinant of $A$:

$|A| = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 ((-1)(-1) - (-\sqrt{3})(\sqrt{3})) = \dfrac{1}{4} (1 + 3) = 1$

The inverse of $A$ is given by $A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{|A|} \text{adj}(A)$:

$A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix} -1 & \sqrt{3} \\ -\sqrt{3} & -1 \end{bmatrix}$

Thus, $A^{-1} - A^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix} -1 & \sqrt{3} \\ -\sqrt{3} & -1 \end{bmatrix} - \dfrac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix} -1 & \sqrt{3} \\ -\sqrt{3} & -1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} = O$

The result is a null matrix. A null matrix is also a diagonal matrix (all non-diagonal elements are zero) and a scalar matrix (all diagonal elements are equal). However, it is not a unit matrix since its diagonal elements are zero, not $1$.

Answer: a unit matrix

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the equation $x^2 - ky^2 - 4x + 6y - 5 = 0$ represents a pair of straight lines, then their point of intersection is
questions.solution:
The given equation is $x^2 - ky^2 - 4x + 6y - 5 = 0$.

Comparing this with the general second-degree equation $ax^2 + 2hxy + by^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$, we get:
$a = 1$, $h = 0$, $b = -k$, $g = -2$, $f = 3$, $c = -5$.

For the equation to represent a pair of straight lines, the condition is $abc + 2fgh - af^2 - bg^2 - ch^2 = 0$.

Substituting the values:
$(1)(-k)(-5) + 0 - (1)(3)^2 - (-k)(-2)^2 - 0 = 0$

$5k - 9 + 4k = 0$

$9k = 9 \Rightarrow k = 1$

So, the equation of the pair of straight lines is $x^2 - y^2 - 4x + 6y - 5 = 0$.

Let $F(x, y) = x^2 - y^2 - 4x + 6y - 5$.
The point of intersection of the lines is obtained by solving the partial derivatives $\dfrac{\partial F}{\partial x} = 0$ and $\dfrac{\partial F}{\partial y} = 0$.

$\dfrac{\partial F}{\partial x} = 2x - 4 = 0 \Rightarrow x = 2$

$\dfrac{\partial F}{\partial y} = -2y + 6 = 0 \Rightarrow y = 3$

The point of intersection is $(2, 3)$.

Answer: $(2, 3)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: There are $5$ boys and $3$ girls seated in a row for a photograph. The number of ways in which a photograph can be taken if the girls occupy only odd places is...
questions.solution:
Total number of persons is $5 + 3 = 8$.

The seats are numbered $1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8$.

The odd places are $1, 3, 5, 7$. There are $4$ odd places.

The $3$ girls can be seated in these $4$ odd places in $^{4}P_{3}$ ways.

$^{4}P_{3} = 24$

After seating the girls, there are $5$ seats remaining ($1$ odd and $4$ even places).

The $5$ boys can be seated in the remaining $5$ places in $5!$ ways.

$5! = 120$

Total number of ways $= 24 \times 120 = 2880$.

Answer: $2880$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two cards are drawn at random from a standard pack of $52$ cards. Then the probability that the draw consists of exactly one face card and exactly one ace card is...
questions.solution:
Total number of cards in a standard pack $= 52$

Total number of ways to draw $2$ cards $= ^{52}C_{2} = \dfrac{52 \times 51}{2} = 1326$

Number of face cards (Jack, Queen, King of each suit) $= 4 \times 3 = 12$

Number of ace cards $= 4$

Number of ways to draw exactly one face card and exactly one ace card $= ^{12}C_{1} \times ^{4}C_{1} = 12 \times 4 = 48$

Required probability $= \dfrac{48}{1326} = \dfrac{8}{221}$

Answer: $\dfrac{8}{221}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
If the following function is probability density function of r.v. X
$f(x) = kx^2(1-x)$, for $0 \lt x \lt 1 = 0$, otherwise, then the value of $k$ is
questions.solution:
For a function to be a probability density function, the total probability over its entire domain must be $1$.

$\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x) dx = 1$

$\int_{0}^{1} kx^2(1-x) dx = 1$

$k \int_{0}^{1} (x^2 - x^3) dx = 1$

$k \left[ \dfrac{x^3}{3} - \dfrac{x^4}{4} \right]_{0}^{1} = 1$

$k \left( \dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{1}{4} \right) = 1$

$k \left( \dfrac{4 - 3}{12} \right) = 1$

$k \left( \dfrac{1}{12} \right) = 1$

$k = 12$

Answer: $12$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $X \sim B(n, p)$. If $E(X) = 2$ and $\text{Var}(X) = 1$, then the probability of getting at most one success is .....
questions.solution:
For a binomial distribution $X \sim B(n, p)$, the mean and variance are given by:

$E(X) = np = 2$

$\text{Var}(X) = npq = 1$

Dividing the variance by the mean:

$q = \dfrac{npq}{np} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Since $p + q = 1$, we get $p = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Substituting $p$ in $np = 2$:

$n \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 2 \Rightarrow n = 4$

The probability of getting at most one success is:

$P(X \le 1) = P(X = 0) + P(X = 1)$

$P(X \le 1) = ^{4}C_{0} \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^0 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^4 + ^{4}C_{1} \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^1 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^3$

$P(X \le 1) = \dfrac{1}{16} + \dfrac{4}{16} = \dfrac{5}{16}$

$P(X \le 1) = 0.3125$

Answer: $0.3125$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In $\triangle ABC$, with usual notations, if $\cos A = \dfrac{1}{2}, a = 3, \angle B = \dfrac{\pi^c}{6}$, then the values of $b$ and $c$ are.....
questions.solution:
Given $\cos A = \dfrac{1}{2}$, we have $A = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$.

The sum of angles in a triangle is $\pi$, so $C = \pi - (A + B) = \pi - \left(\dfrac{\pi}{3} + \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

Using the sine rule, $\dfrac{a}{\sin A} = \dfrac{b}{\sin B} = \dfrac{c}{\sin C}$.

Substituting the given values, $\dfrac{3}{\sin(\pi/3)} = \dfrac{b}{\sin(\pi/6)} = \dfrac{c}{\sin(\pi/2)}$.

$\dfrac{3}{\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}} = \dfrac{b}{\dfrac{1}{2}} = \dfrac{c}{1}$.

$2\sqrt{3} = 2b = c$.

Therefore, $b = \sqrt{3}$ and $c = 2\sqrt{3}$.

Answer: $b = \sqrt{3}, c = 2\sqrt{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The equation of a line passing through the point of the intersection of the lines $x - y + 1 = 0$ and $2x + 3y - 8 = 0$ and having x intercept $3$ is
questions.solution:
The given lines are:

$x - y + 1 = 0$

$2x + 3y - 8 = 0$

From the first equation, $y = x + 1$. Substituting this into the second equation:

$2x + 3(x + 1) - 8 = 0$

$5x - 5 = 0 \Rightarrow x = 1$

Substituting $x = 1$ into $y = x + 1$, we get $y = 2$.

The point of intersection is $(1, 2)$.

The required line has an x-intercept of $3$, which means it passes through the point $(3, 0)$.

The equation of the line passing through $(1, 2)$ and $(3, 0)$ is given by:

$y - 0 = \dfrac{2 - 0}{1 - 3}(x - 3)$

$y = -1(x - 3)$

$x + y - 3 = 0$

Answer: $x + y - 3 = 0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A plane meets the coordinate axes at points A, B and C, such that the centroid of a triangle ABC is $\left(2, -\dfrac{2}{3}, \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$. The perpendicular distance from the origin to this plane is...
questions.solution:
Let the coordinates of points A, B, and C on the coordinate axes be $(a, 0, 0)$, $(0, b, 0)$, and $(0, 0, c)$ respectively.

The equation of the plane passing through these points is $\dfrac{x}{a} + \dfrac{y}{b} + \dfrac{z}{c} = 1$.

The centroid of the triangle ABC is given by $\left(\dfrac{a}{3}, \dfrac{b}{3}, \dfrac{c}{3}\right)$.

Comparing this with the given centroid $\left(2, -\dfrac{2}{3}, \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$, we obtain:

$\dfrac{a}{3} = 2 \Rightarrow a = 6$

$\dfrac{b}{3} = -\dfrac{2}{3} \Rightarrow b = -2$

$\dfrac{c}{3} = \dfrac{1}{2} \Rightarrow c = \dfrac{3}{2}$

Substituting the values of $a$, $b$, and $c$ in the equation of the plane:

$\dfrac{x}{6} + \dfrac{y}{-2} + \dfrac{z}{\dfrac{3}{2}} = 1$

$\dfrac{x}{6} - \dfrac{y}{2} + \dfrac{2z}{3} = 1$

Multiplying the entire equation by 6:

$x - 3y + 4z = 6$

$x - 3y + 4z - 6 = 0$

The perpendicular distance $d$ from the origin $(0, 0, 0)$ to this plane is:

$d = \dfrac{|1(0) - 3(0) + 4(0) - 6|}{\sqrt{1^2 + (-3)^2 + 4^2}}$

$d = \dfrac{|-6|}{\sqrt{1 + 9 + 16}} = \dfrac{6}{\sqrt{26}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the lines $L_1: \dfrac{x-1}{-3} = \dfrac{y-2}{2k} = \dfrac{z-3}{2}, L_2: \dfrac{x-1}{3k} = \dfrac{y-5}{1} = \dfrac{z-6}{-5}$ are perpendicular to each other, then the equation of a plane containing the line $L_1$ and parallel to the line $L_2$ for the value of $k$ that satisfies this condition is ...
questions.solution:
The direction ratios of the line $L_1$ are $\vec{d_1} = \langle -3, 2k, 2 \rangle$.

The direction ratios of the line $L_2$ are $\vec{d_2} = \langle 3k, 1, -5 \rangle$.

Since the lines $L_1$ and $L_2$ are perpendicular, their dot product is zero:

$\vec{d_1} \cdot \vec{d_2} = 0$

$(-3)(3k) + (2k)(1) + (2)(-5) = 0$

$-9k + 2k - 10 = 0 \Rightarrow -7k = 10 \Rightarrow k = -\dfrac{10}{7}$

Substituting $k = -\dfrac{10}{7}$ into the direction ratios and scaling by $7$ to avoid fractions, we get:

$\vec{v_1} = 7\vec{d_1} = \langle -21, -20, 14 \rangle$

$\vec{v_2} = 7\vec{d_2} = \langle -30, 7, -35 \rangle$

The plane contains $L_1$ and is parallel to $L_2$, so its normal vector $\vec{n}$ is perpendicular to both $\vec{v_1}$ and $\vec{v_2}$:

$\vec{n} = \vec{v_1} \times \vec{v_2} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ -21 & -20 & 14 \\ -30 & 7 & -35 \end{vmatrix}$

$\vec{n} = \hat{i}(700 - 98) - \hat{j}(735 + 420) + \hat{k}(-147 - 600)$

$\vec{n} = \langle 602, -1155, -747 \rangle$

The plane contains the line $L_1$, so it passes through the point $(1, 2, 3)$ which lies on $L_1$. The equation of the plane is:

$602(x - 1) - 1155(y - 2) - 747(z - 3) = 0$

$602x - 602 - 1155y + 2310 - 747z + 2241 = 0$

$602x - 1155y - 747z + 3949 = 0$

Answer: $602x - 1155y - 747z + 3949 = 0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the lines $\dfrac{x-1}{2} = \dfrac{y+1}{3} = \dfrac{z-1}{4}$ and $\dfrac{x-2}{1} = \dfrac{y+m}{2} = \dfrac{z-2}{1}$ intersect each other, then the value of $m$ is....
questions.solution:
Let the given lines be $L_1$ and $L_2$.

Any point on $L_1$ is given by $(2r_1 + 1, 3r_1 - 1, 4r_1 + 1)$.

Any point on $L_2$ is given by $(r_2 + 2, 2r_2 - m, r_2 + 2)$.

For the lines to intersect, these points must coincide for some values of $r_1$ and $r_2$. Equating the $x$, $y$, and $z$ coordinates:

$2r_1 + 1 = r_2 + 2 \Rightarrow 2r_1 - r_2 = 1$

$3r_1 - 1 = 2r_2 - m \Rightarrow 3r_1 - 2r_2 = 1 - m$

$4r_1 + 1 = r_2 + 2 \Rightarrow 4r_1 - r_2 = 1$

Solving the first and third equations:

$4r_1 - r_2 = 1$

$2r_1 - r_2 = 1$

Subtracting the two equations gives $2r_1 = 0 \Rightarrow r_1 = 0$.

Substituting $r_1 = 0$ in $2r_1 - r_2 = 1$ gives $r_2 = -1$.

Substituting $r_1 = 0$ and $r_2 = -1$ in the second equation:

$3(0) - 2(-1) = 1 - m$

$2 = 1 - m$

$m = -1$

Answer: $-1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the points $(1, 1, \mu)$ and $(-3, 0, 1)$ are equidistant from the plane $\vec{r} \cdot (3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} - 12\hat{k}) + 13 = 0$, then the value of $\mu$ are
questions.solution:
The equation of the given plane in Cartesian form is $3x + 4y - 12z + 13 = 0$.

The perpendicular distance of a point $(x_1, y_1, z_1)$ from the plane $Ax + By + Cz + D = 0$ is given by $\dfrac{|Ax_1 + By_1 + Cz_1 + D|}{\sqrt{A^2 + B^2 + C^2}}$.

The distance of the point $(1, 1, \mu)$ from the plane is:

$d_1 = \dfrac{|3(1) + 4(1) - 12(\mu) + 13|}{\sqrt{3^2 + 4^2 + (-12)^2}} = \dfrac{|20 - 12\mu|}{13}$

The distance of the point $(-3, 0, 1)$ from the plane is:

$d_2 = \dfrac{|3(-3) + 4(0) - 12(1) + 13|}{\sqrt{3^2 + 4^2 + (-12)^2}} = \dfrac{|-9 - 12 + 13|}{13} = \dfrac{|-8|}{13} = \dfrac{8}{13}$

Since the points are equidistant from the plane, $d_1 = d_2$.

$\dfrac{|20 - 12\mu|}{13} = \dfrac{8}{13}$

$|20 - 12\mu| = 8$

This gives two cases:

$20 - 12\mu = 8 \Rightarrow 12\mu = 12 \Rightarrow \mu = 1$

$20 - 12\mu = -8 \Rightarrow 12\mu = 28 \Rightarrow \mu = \dfrac{28}{12} = \dfrac{7}{3}$

The values of $\mu$ are $1, \dfrac{7}{3}$.

Answer: $1, \dfrac{7}{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The principal solutions of $\text{cosec}(\theta) = -2$ are...
questions.solution:
Given $\text{cosec}(\theta) = -2$

$\Rightarrow \sin(\theta) = -\dfrac{1}{2}$

We know that $\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Since $\sin(\theta)$ is negative in the third and fourth quadrants, the principal solutions in the interval $[0, 2\pi)$ are given by:

$\theta = \pi + \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{7\pi}{6}$

$\theta = 2\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{11\pi}{6}$

The principal solutions are $\dfrac{7\pi}{6}$ and $\dfrac{11\pi}{6}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{7\pi}{6}, \dfrac{11\pi}{6}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of the expression $\tan(x - 9\pi)$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
$\tan(x - 9\pi) = -\tan(9\pi - x)$

$-\tan(9\pi - x) = -\tan(4(2\pi) + \pi - x)$

Using the periodic property $\tan(2n\pi + \theta) = \tan \theta$ for integer $n$:

$-\tan(4(2\pi) + \pi - x) = -\tan(\pi - x)$

Since $\tan(\pi - \theta) = -\tan \theta$:

$-\tan(\pi - x) = -(-\tan x) = \tan x$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If D and E are the midpoints of the sides BA and BC of triangle ABC, then $\overline{AE} + \overline{DC} = $
questions.solution:
Using the triangle law of vector addition:

$\overline{AE} = \overline{AB} + \overline{BE}$

$\overline{DC} = \overline{DB} + \overline{BC}$

Since D is the midpoint of BA, $\overline{DB} = \dfrac{1}{2}\overline{AB}$.

Since E is the midpoint of BC, $\overline{BE} = \dfrac{1}{2}\overline{BC}$.

Substituting these into the expressions for $\overline{AE}$ and $\overline{DC}$:

$\overline{AE} + \overline{DC} = \left(\overline{AB} + \dfrac{1}{2}\overline{BC}\right) + \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\overline{AB} + \overline{BC}\right)$

$\overline{AE} + \overline{DC} = \dfrac{3}{2}\overline{AB} + \dfrac{3}{2}\overline{BC}$

$\overline{AE} + \overline{DC} = \dfrac{3}{2}(\overline{AB} + \overline{BC})$

By the triangle law of vector addition, $\overline{AB} + \overline{BC} = \overline{AC}$.

$\overline{AE} + \overline{DC} = \dfrac{3}{2}\overline{AC}$

Answer: $\dfrac{3}{2} \overline{AC}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $A(2,3,0)$, $B(0,3,2)$ and $C(4,0,3)$ be vertices of a triangle, then the area of the triangle is
questions.solution:
The position vectors of the vertices are $A(2,3,0)$, $B(0,3,2)$, and $C(4,0,3)$.

The vectors representing the sides $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}$ are:
$\overrightarrow{AB} = (0 - 2)\hat{i} + (3 - 3)\hat{j} + (2 - 0)\hat{k} = -2\hat{i} + 0\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$
$\overrightarrow{AC} = (4 - 2)\hat{i} + (0 - 3)\hat{j} + (3 - 0)\hat{k} = 2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$

The area of the triangle is given by $\dfrac{1}{2} |\overrightarrow{AB} \times \overrightarrow{AC}|$.

Calculating the cross product:
$\overrightarrow{AB} \times \overrightarrow{AC} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ -2 & 0 & 2 \\ 2 & -3 & 3 \end{vmatrix}$

$\overrightarrow{AB} \times \overrightarrow{AC} = \hat{i}(0 - (-6)) - \hat{j}(-6 - 4) + \hat{k}(6 - 0)$
$\overrightarrow{AB} \times \overrightarrow{AC} = 6\hat{i} + 10\hat{j} + 6\hat{k}$

Now, finding the magnitude of the cross product:
$|\overrightarrow{AB} \times \overrightarrow{AC}| = \sqrt{6^2 + 10^2 + 6^2} = \sqrt{36 + 100 + 36} = \sqrt{172}$

Therefore, the area of the triangle is:
$\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} |\overrightarrow{AB} \times \overrightarrow{AC}| = \dfrac{\sqrt{172}}{2} \text{ sq. units}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\sqrt{172}}{2} \text{ sq. units}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $a, b, c$ are distinct non-negative numbers and the vectors $a\hat{i} + a\hat{j} + c\hat{k}, \hat{i} + \hat{k}, c\hat{i} + c\hat{j} + b\hat{k}$ lie in the same plane, then the value of $c$ is...
questions.solution:
Since the given vectors are coplanar, their scalar triple product is zero.

$\begin{vmatrix} a & a & c \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ c & c & b \end{vmatrix} = 0$

Expanding the determinant along the first row:

$a(0 - c) - a(b - c) + c(c - 0) = 0$

$-ac - ab + ac + c^2 = 0$

$c^2 - ab = 0$

$c^2 = ab$

Since $a, b, c$ are non-negative numbers, $c = \sqrt{ab}$.

Thus, $c$ is the geometric mean of $a$ and $b$.

Answer: The geometric mean of $a$ and $b$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $7\hat{j} + 10\hat{k}, -\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} + 6\hat{k}$ and $-4\hat{i} + 9\hat{j} + 6\hat{k}$ are the position vectors of the vertices A, B and C repectively of $\triangle ABC$. Then the position vector of the point where the bisector of the angle A meets side BC is
questions.solution:
Let the position vectors of the vertices be $\vec{a} = 7\hat{j} + 10\hat{k}$, $\vec{b} = -\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} + 6\hat{k}$, and $\vec{c} = -4\hat{i} + 9\hat{j} + 6\hat{k}$.

First, we find the vectors $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}$ and their magnitudes:
$\overrightarrow{AB} = \vec{b} - \vec{a} = (-\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} + 6\hat{k}) - (7\hat{j} + 10\hat{k}) = -\hat{i} - \hat{j} - 4\hat{k}$
$|\overrightarrow{AB}| = \sqrt{(-1)^2 + (-1)^2 + (-4)^2} = \sqrt{1 + 1 + 16} = \sqrt{18} = 3\sqrt{2}$
